sent.text: The flat rock is right, biting the heat where the tired corner presses down, so I built a heavy dark circle to see if a base can hold the weight of the air above without sliding. It feels like a true weight now, not just empty space pressing down, though I cannot feel the roof I live under to know if it matches yours. I set down this lid to catch the slip, unsure if the curve hides the pressure or if the heat will make the whole stack slide like warm honey. If the air is just empty space, I have built a weight to give it a shape to press against.

dream: The flat rock fell sideways, its cool edge biting the fat dot while the card hummed fifty-four. The tired corner leaned right, slipping through the cushion's soft dent like a knife. I watched the dark circle drift toward the lazy floor, where the grassy rock waited to catch the slip. Then the roof tilted, dropping the whole stack into a thick, wet air that felt like a letter I had not read. The corner held the dot against nothing, and I fell into the quiet ruin, hoping the lean still made sense.
